Run `cargo test -p athena-core role_need`.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md names the root cause (usage measure blind to roles whose runs are outside job records) and the fix.
criteria.evidence: The CHANGELOG entry says: "Root cause fixed: a usage measure was written against one data source, the per-job invocation list, so roles whose runs are outside job records (the steward, audience and auditor) looked unused ... `Records::all_invocations` now yields every run source".

findings.summary: The measure was not replayed over the real records. On them it would advise retiring the auditor, which the request names as known-active.
findings.evidence: Evidence snapshot, read with Glob and Grep; this is a result about the snapshot, not the live repository. The newest 8 closed jobs that count as work are 20261110-191432-ysr1, 20261111-022136-czdw, 055238-5har, 061100-smxs, 064834-q749, 075222-nsk3, 105048-n7bm and 122652-1k8z (landed, rejected and failed outcomes). Steward runs (20261111-055051, 061048), audience runs, and planner and critic runs (191432-ysr1, 064834-q749) fall inside the window. The only auditor invocations are jobs/2026-10/20261017-201222-3a9h and 20261017-200939-4ynn. So status would print "role need  retire candidates: auditor ...". The request's cause lists the auditor among roles "known" to be active and says the missing step was replay "on the real records" and comparison "with known facts". The auditor runs on demand (`athena audit`), so a fixed 8-job window may not show whether it is needed. The fix needs either a replay against the known-active list or a "not measured" / on-demand case, as introspection 20261111-105017-5k6m proposed. `status --snapshot` does not print role need, so the snapshot cannot show the line.

findings.summary: The class fix is an opt-in accessor. Nothing points a future measure to it or stops one from using the partial source, so the class is not prevented.
findings.evidence: `pub invocations: Vec<Invocation>` on JobRecords still has no doc comment saying the steward, audience and auditor runs are not in it. The only pointer is on the new all_invocations, which a writer reaching for job.invocations will not see. docs/system-facts.md has no mention of steward, audience, auditor or invocation (Grep: no matches). The request prefers giving the stage this information in its brief or system facts. Introspection 5k6m names "The producer was not told where each role's runs are recorded". No test or check requires a new measure to be replayed over real records, and no store-level test checks that all_invocations covers every loaded invocation (one would catch a future fourth split list). Simpler and stronger options: document the split on JobRecords::invocations and in the system facts, and add a test over Records::from_parts that every Invocation record appears in all_invocations.

findings.summary: Dropped, stale and abandoned jobs count as worked, non-failed jobs in both the window and the per-class totals.
findings.evidence: counts_as_work excludes only Declined and Closed. The snapshot holds 111 dropped and 14 stale jobs (from `status --snapshot`). Jobs that never ran a model can enter the window and pad the "closed" total of "code N/8 failed".

findings.summary: The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met
findings.evidence: The request asks for the cause to be fixed where it originates "so the whole class is prevented", preferably by giving the failing stage the missing information "in its brief, in the system facts it is shown, or in the inputs its reader receives". The cause it quotes includes "Nothing required it to be run on the real records, or compared with known facts such as the steward, audience and auditor being active". The reading narrowed this to one accessor plus one measure and claimed the accessor means "a new measure cannot pick a partial source". That is not true: JobRecords::invocations is still public and undocumented, nothing points a measure author to all_invocations, the system facts are unchanged, and no replay over real records against known-active roles is required or done. The criteria therefore check one fixed instance, not prevention of the class.

summary: The candidate adds Records::all_invocations and a role_need measure built on it, with tests showing steward, audience and auditor runs kept outside the jobs are counted. All seven acceptance criteria are met as written and the targeted tests pass. It still fails the request, which asks to fix the cause so the whole class is prevented. (1) The stated cause includes that nothing required a measure to be replayed over the real records and compared with known-active roles. The candidate did neither. I traced the measure by hand over the evidence snapshot: its window runs from 20261110-191432-ysr1 to 20261111-122652-1k8z, and the auditor's only runs are from 2026-10-17. So `athena status` on the real records would print "role need  retire candidates: auditor", a role the request calls known-active. (2) The class-level fix is an opt-in accessor. JobRecords::invocations stays public with no warning, docs/system-facts.md says nothing about where each role's runs are recorded, and no check requires a replay. The next usage measure could repeat the failure. Minor issues: dropped, stale and abandoned jobs count as non-failed work, and two changed files were not on the deliverables list.
